projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained 24–26 connected devices paired with zero camera motion at 11:17 PM on a Saturday strongly indicates a quiet indoor gathering or winding-down period where everyone is in a darkened, camera-obscured area. This coherent pattern explains the high device count without triggering motion alerts and aligns with typical Saturday night behavior.

The sustained 20–25 device count on a Saturday evening with zero camera motion strongly suggests a social gathering in camera-blind zones or with cameras temporarily disabled; verify this is a planned event to rule out unauthorized access.

The sustained connection of 20–25 mobile devices paired with zero camera motion over several hours strongly indicates a large gathering or party where guests are occupying non-camera areas, or multiple devices are left stationary in unmonitored rooms, warranting a quick check to confirm if the family is hosting or if there's a network anomaly.

The sustained 20–25 device count paired with zero camera motion strongly suggests the presence data is tracking stationary IoT devices, parked vehicles, or neighbor Wi-Fi bleed rather than active human occupancy, which may be causing home automations to run on false occupancy assumptions.

The sustained presence of 20–25 devices with zero camera motion on a Saturday evening strongly suggests either a quiet gathering where guests are avoiding camera view (e.g., garage, backyard, or cameras disabled for privacy) or that the count is inflated by stationary IoT devices rather than active people. This matters because it may indicate a false presence alert or a privacy-conscious event that warrants a quick status check.

The sustained presence of 24–27 devices paired with zero camera motion over four hours strongly suggests either the security cameras are offline or the presence system is miscounting IoT devices, leaving the home unmonitored despite appearing occupied.

The sustained high device count (21–26) paired with zero camera activity on a Saturday afternoon indicates an indoor gathering or IoT devices being counted as mobile users, which is consistent with typical weekend household activity.

The consistently high presence count (23–26) paired with zero camera activity confirms the presence system is counting IoT network traffic rather than human occupancy, indicating a normal, quiet weekend morning rather than a gathering or anomaly.

The consistently high presence count (23-25 devices) paired with zero camera activity indicates a quiet, stationary Saturday indoors, likely involving guests or smart home devices being counted as mobile. This is normal for a weekend but worth verifying if the device count seems unexpectedly high.

The sustained presence of 21-24 mobile devices combined with zero camera, lighting, or activity signals overnight strongly indicates devices are stationary and charging rather than active use or unauthorized presence.
